core_intuitions: The '~$100 model' is an accounting, not a slogan: it itemizes to ~39 GPU-hours across all stages (~$1.80/GPU-hr) plus ~$13 non-GPU (teacher API + storage) plus a ~25% re-run reality tax; pretraining is ~40% of the bill and OVER-TRAINING is ~90% of the pretraining line by deliberate choice.

Over-training is inference-aware, not wasteful: you pay training compute ONCE (6ND) but save inference compute (2ND per request) FOREVER; because served FLOPs dwarf the one-time pretrain, the extra ~$36 spent over-training buys a permanently cheaper-to-serve model and pays for itself many times over at deployment scale.

Cost = FLOPs / (MFU x peak): the 6ND rule fixes the FLOP floor; MFU is the sustained/peak fraction (deep-thin Stack-100M sits low, ~0.45); always compute the bill from MEASURED tokens/sec and quote $/GPU-hr AND MFU alongside the dollar figure or it is not reproducible.

Reproducibility = five pillars welded into a self-describing checkpoint: seed STATE (not just the integer), config hash, content-addressed data manifest, environment pin (fail on a dirty git tree), and atomic checkpoints - all validated by a hermetic 50-step CPU run that must reproduce bit-for-bit.

Scaling 100M->1B: DATA breaks first (need 200B-1T tokens; repetition past ~4 epochs does not substitute), then TIME breaks (1B still fits one 80GB A100 at ~16 B/param, but the run is ~100x longer) - so climb the parallelism ladder DP -> FSDP -> tensor/pipeline only as far as the model forces you; at 1B, DDP is enough and pipeline is premature.

MoE is the fork beyond 1B: fine-grained routed experts + always-on shared experts decouple TOTAL capacity (quality) from ACTIVE params (compute/token/latency), so N_total >> N_active - but you pay for it in memory (all experts resident) and all-to-all communication, making it a serving decision, not a free lunch.

new_figures.name: capstone-cost-anatomy
new_figures.concept: Where the ~$100 actually goes, stage by stage, with over-training exposed as the dominant sub-chunk of the pretraining line and the teacher API / re-run tax as the hidden extras.
new_figures.rationale: This is the concrete deliverable of section 14.12.2 and the whole 'landing the plane' promise - the headline '$100 model' only means something once you SEE the anatomy. The chapter's central lessons (pretraining is ~40% and over-training is most of it; the teacher API is a non-GPU surprise; the re-run tax is real) are all quantitative-comparative and land far harder as one bar than as a table. It is the single most foundational figure for this chapter and the chapter has none.
new_figures.brief: A single static infographic that turns the itemized bill into a visual anatomy building to ~$100. PRIMARY ELEMENT - one horizontal stacked cost bar (full width) whose total length reads as ~$100, segmented left-to-right into the chapter's own line items (use ONLY the chapter's figures; invent none): a big PRETRAIN segment (~$39.60), then mid-training (~$8.10), scaling-law ladder (~$8.10), agent distillation (~$9.80), GRPO (~$5.40), SFT+DPO+eval/quant+tokenizer (group the small ones, ~$8.66 total), storage+egress (~$5.00), and a final RE-RUN REALITY TAX segment (~$17.40). Group and tint the segments by CATEGORY - one accent family for GPU-compute stages, a second accent for NON-GPU items (teacher API, storage), a third muted accent for the re-run tax - with a small legend. KEY ANNOTATION 1: split the pretrain segment internally with a thin divider into 'Chinchilla-optimal floor (~$4)' vs 'deliberate over-training (~$36)', and label it 'over-training = ~90% of the pretrain line, bought back at serving time'. KEY ANNOTATION 2: pull a callout from the agent-distillation segment noting '$8 of this is teacher API, NOT your GPU - at 1B this can exceed your own training cost'. KEY ANNOTATION 3: label the re-run tax segment '~25% for OOMs, bad launches, 2 restarts - the gap between sticker and invoice'. Optionally add a compact secondary panel or side note stating the price sensitivity: 'total is a BAND $40-$100; the ~2.5x spread is entirely $/GPU-hr and how many times you fat-finger a launch - always quote $/GPU-hr + MFU'. Theme-safe: category accents distinct in both light and dark, all $ labels and dividers legible, no overlapping text; the eye should read total -> dominant pretrain segment -> the over-training split -> the two hidden extras. Everything within the viewBox; a single static frame conveys it fully.

new_figures.name: capstone-pay-once-save-forever
new_figures.concept: The inference-aware over-training asymmetry: training compute (6ND) is paid ONCE, inference compute (2ND/request) is paid FOREVER, so a modest over-training investment that keeps the model small saves far more served FLOPs than it cost.
new_figures.rationale: This is named the chapter's single most important lesson ('deliberate over-training') and it recurs in the cost table, the worked example, and the scale-up section - yet it is an economic asymmetry that a static comparison makes visceral in a way the algebra does not. It is distinct from the scaling-laws chapter's 'optimum slides with tokens/param' figure: here the intuition is a break-even LEDGER tied to the $100 bill (spend ~$36 once, save ~a full pretrain budget per billion requests). Foundational to why the whole capstone over-trained on ~20B tokens.
new_figures.placement: Worked example: does over-training actually pay off?
new_figures.brief: A static ledger/balance infographic contrasting a ONE-TIME cost against a REPEATING saving. Structure it as two facing columns or a balance-scale motif. LEFT (paid once): a single block 'Training compute = 6 N D_train, paid ONCE' with the chapter's illustrative pretrain figure (~1.2 x 10^19 FLOPs, ~$40, with the over-training portion ~$36 highlighted as 'the extra you chose to spend'). RIGHT (paid forever): a repeating stack of small blocks 'Inference = 2 N D per request, paid EVERY request', fanning out to show accumulation across requests; annotate one representative scale from the chapter - '1 billion requests x 256 tokens ~ 5.2 x 10^19 FLOPs served' - and note that this is ~4x the entire pretraining budget. CENTER / PAYOFF: an arrow or fulcrum showing the trade - 'over-training kept the model at 100M instead of needing ~200M (roughly 2x serve FLOPs); the ~$36 saves ~one full pretrain-budget of compute PER BILLION requests'. Add a compact governing line: 'lifetime compute = 6 N D_train (once) + 2 N D_inf (forever); heavier serving -> over-train harder'. Make the asymmetry the visual punchline: the left block is fixed and finite, the right stack visibly outgrows it as requests accumulate. Use ONLY the chapter's illustrative magnitudes; invent no others; axes/counts are schematic. Theme-safe: one accent for the one-time training cost, a second for the repeating inference saving, theme ink for labels; legible in both themes, no overlaps, all within the viewBox. A single static frame (finite block vs growing stack) conveys it; no animation needed.

new_figures.name: capstone-scaleup-ladder
new_figures.concept: What breaks first when you run the exact 100M recipe at 1B - data volume, then wall-clock time (NOT single-GPU memory) - and the parallelism ladder DP -> FSDP -> tensor/pipeline you climb only as far as the model forces you.
new_figures.rationale: Section 14.12.4 is the chapter's forward-looking payload and its core message is a WALL-ORDERING plus a discipline ('climb the ladder only as forced; at 1B DDP is enough, pipeline is premature'). That ordering - data wall before time wall before memory wall, and each parallelism rung unlocked by a specific failure - is exactly the kind of gated progression a single static figure makes memorable where scattered prose does not. Serves three intuitions at once (data-first, time-not-memory, complexity-ladder).
new_figures.placement: 14.12.4 What Breaks at 1B - and What to Change
new_figures.brief: A static figure combining a WALL-ORDER timeline with a PARALLELISM LADDER. TOP STRIP - 'what breaks, in the order you hit it': three gates left-to-right. Gate 1 DATA WALL (breaks FIRST): '~20B tokens is 10-50x too small; 1B wants 200B-1T; repetition helps only to ~4 epochs, collapses by ~16' -> fix: 'full FineWeb + real dedup/quality/mix'. Gate 2 TIME WALL: '1B over 200B tokens ~ 1.2 x 10^21 FLOPs ~ 100x the capstone pretrain = thousands of GPU-hr on one card'. Gate 3 (drawn as a wall you DON'T hit at 1B, e.g. greyed / crossed out) MEMORY: 'at 16 B/param, 1B = ~16 GB -> STILL FITS one 80GB A100; memory is NOT the 1B blocker'. Make explicit that the recipe breaks on TIME, not memory, at 1B. BOTTOM - the parallelism ladder as three ascending rungs, each labeled with the trigger that forces you up: Rung 1 'DDP / data parallelism - replicate, split batch, all-reduce grads; near-linear while the model FITS per GPU -> USE THIS AT 1B (8xA100 turns thousands of GPU-hr into hundreds)'. Rung 2 'FSDP / ZeRO - shard params+grads+opt (1/g of 16 B/param); needed when it stops fitting (~7B+); at 1B only a convenience for bigger batch'. Rung 3 'Tensor + Pipeline - split matmuls / stage layers; pure comm+bubble overhead; only at tens of B+ -> DO NOT reach for this at 1B'. Visually mark the 'you are here at 1B' position on Rung 1 and grey Rungs 2-3 as 'not yet'. Include the memory-fits mini-table from the chapter as a small inset (0.1B->1.6GB fits, 1B->16GB fits, 7B->112GB no, 70B->1120GB cluster) using ONLY those chapter figures. Governing caption: 'climb the ladder only as far as the model forces you'. Theme-safe: distinct accents for the three walls vs the three rungs, the 'grey/crossed' state must read as inactive in BOTH light and dark, all labels legible, clear reading order (top walls left-to-right, then ladder bottom-up), everything within the viewBox. Static frame suffices.

new_figures.name: capstone-moe-capacity-vs-compute
new_figures.concept: The MoE fork: fine-grained routed experts + always-on shared experts let TOTAL capacity (parameters, sets quality) far exceed ACTIVE params per token (FLOPs, sets latency) - at the cost of resident memory and all-to-all routing.
new_figures.rationale: The MoE decision is presented as 'the single highest-leverage architecture change beyond 1B' and the whole pitch is one decoupling: N_total >> N_active. A static schematic of one token routed through k experts + shared experts, with the capacity-vs-compute counts made explicit (18 resident, 3 active, sub-dense FFN width), makes the 'more capacity than dense, less compute than dense' claim concrete right where the reader must decide dense-vs-MoE. The full mechanism lives in the MoE chapter, so this stays a decision-focused sketch, not a re-teach - which keeps it a supporting figure.
new_figures.placement: The MoE fork in the road

CENTER: one token vector entering the block. summary: A figure-less, concept-rich retrospective/landing chapter, so this is a pure new-figure plan (no existing figures to audit). The chapter's payload is three things - a cost accounting, a reproducibility discipline, and a 1B scale-up analysis - and the highest-intuition gaps are quantitative-comparative or gated-progression ideas that beg for one strong static each. Priority-1 figures: (1) capstone-cost-anatomy, the itemized ~$100 bill as one stacked bar with over-training, the teacher-API surprise, and the re-run tax exposed - the chapter's central deliverable; (2) capstone-pay-once-save-forever, the inference-aware over-training asymmetry as a break-even ledger (spend once, save forever) tied to the $100 bill and distinct from the scaling-laws chapter's optimum-slide figure; (3) capstone-scaleup-ladder, the what-breaks-first wall ordering (data -> time, NOT memory) plus the DP->FSDP->tensor/pipeline ladder you climb only as forced. Priority-2: (4) capstone-moe-capacity-vs-compute, a decision-focused sketch of N_total >> N_active with the memory+all-to-all catch. Reproducibility (14.12.3) is intentionally left figure-free: its five pillars are already well served by the chapter's provenance code and the one-page preflight checklist, so a figure there would be decoration rather than intuition. All four proposed figures are static - a single frame conveys each - keeping to a disciplined, foundational set.
